text: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is a promising neuromodulation therapy for major depressive disorder (MDD), but reliable predictors of treatment response are lacking. Second-order morphometric similarity networks (MSN-II), which capture higher-order structural covariance patterns, may provide novel predictive biomarkers.
source_label: Second-order morphometric similarity networks predict response to transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in major depressive disorder: a two-center study
